title: ADR-096 — Database incarnation fence before recovery activation
provenance: Engineering refinement of requested restore safety; exact incarnation mechanism not a documented maintainer choice.
qualification: ADR records reproduced SQL recovery bypass; independent restore/ordinary-restart protocol remained incomplete.

questions.q1: Reproduced stale recovery flag became usable after ordinary observation; deployment frequency unmeasured.
questions.q2: No accepted risk of restoring old authority is documented; relaxed download permission timing does not waive restore fencing.
questions.q3: Protects rare restores but also fences every database restart, a normal operational path.
questions.q4: ADR supplies no comparable-project recovery design; do not infer necessity of every downstream witness.
questions.q5: Runtime loses activation-write privilege; trusted recovery administration remains required.
questions.q6: At least three states: unactivated, current incarnation, recovery-blocked; failed restart activation adds operational outage.
questions.q7: Activation/incarnation fields are internal, not useful end-user configuration.

questions.q10: Migration preserves old state as blocked; rolling upgrade and automatic restart recovery were not qualified.
questions.q11: A single explicit recovery epoch/fence can retain the essential protection; compare operational restart cost before expanding it.

rationale: A concrete authority bypass justifies a fence, not unlimited machinery around it.
action: Retain the core guard; qualify normal restart and compare a simpler operator-controlled restore epoch.
